title: Qatar jet, arms sales and golf deal
summary: Documented: the ~$400M Qatari Boeing 747-8 was accepted by the Pentagon on 21 May 2025 for Air Force One use, with reported plans to transfer it to Trump's library foundation by 2029. Also documented: the $1.96B MQ-9B sale (approved 26 Mar 2025, signed 14 May 2025), a Trump-branded golf club and villas inside Qatari Diar's $5.5B Simaisma project (30 Apr 2025), and May 2026 approvals of Patriot ($4.01B) and APKWS ($992.4M) sales to Qatar. Not supported: I found no reporting of 'favorable terms'; the arms approval came about six weeks before the jet story; the $5.5B is the whole masterplan, not the Trump component; and the 2026 sales were emergency Iran-war replenishments. The link between gifts and arms is insinuation based on timing.

sub_claims.statement: Qatar gifted a ~$400M luxury Boeing 747 for Trump to use as Air Force One.
sub_claims.finding: ABC first reported the plan on 11 May 2025: a 747-8 from the Qatari royal family. Hegseth formally accepted it on 21 May 2025. The $400M is a widely repeated estimate that excludes the retrofit cost. The jet was unveiled in June 2026 and flew as Air Force One by July 2026. Qatar first called it a possible 'temporary use' transfer and disputed that it was a gift.

sub_claims.statement: The plane would go to Trump's presidential library after his presidency.
sub_claims.finding: ABC's sources said ownership would pass to the Trump Presidential Library Foundation no later than 1 Jan 2029, with the Air Force paying the transfer costs, and Trump said it would go to his library. As of mid-2026 the destination was reported as uncertain. The suggestion that he might use it as a private citizen is speculation.

sub_claims.statement: At the same time, Qatar was negotiating a $1.96B arms deal with the US.
sub_claims.finding: DSCA notified Congress of a possible $1.96B sale of 8 MQ-9B drones and munitions on 26 Mar 2025. Qatar signed the LOA ('nearly $2 billion') during Trump's 14 May 2025 Doha visit, three days after the jet story broke. The approval came about six weeks before the jet news.

sub_claims.statement: Qatar got 'pretty favorable terms' on the arms deal, per independent reporting.
sub_claims.finding: I found no reporting that the MQ-9B terms were unusually favourable. The documented context is that the Biden administration had not authorised the sale, Trump's State Department approved it quickly, and it would be the first MQ-9B sale to the Middle East. No evidence ties the sale to the jet.

sub_claims.statement: The Trump family struck a luxury golf course deal in Qatar as part of a ~$5.5B project.
sub_claims.finding: On 30 Apr 2025, Qatari Diar (a subsidiary of the Qatar Investment Authority) signed with Dar Global to develop the Trump International Golf Club and Trump Villas in Simaisma. The $5.5B is the whole Simaisma masterplan, not the Trump component. The Trump Organization licenses its brand through Saudi-linked Dar Global.

sub_claims.statement: In 2026 the State Department approved two more possible sales to Qatar worth ~$5B (APKWS and Patriot replenishment).
sub_claims.finding: Around 1-2 May 2026, State approved Patriot replenishment for about $4.01B (200 PAC-2 GEM-T and 300 PAC-3 MSE) and 10,000 APKWS II rounds for about $992.4M, roughly $5.0B in total. Rubio invoked emergency authority to waive congressional review, citing the Iran conflict that began on 28 Feb 2026.

corrections: Claimed: the arms deal was 'at the same time' as the jet. The record shows: State approved the MQ-9B sale on 26 Mar 2025, about six weeks before the 11 May 2025 jet reports. It was signed on 14 May 2025.

Claimed: the golf deal was part of a '$5.5 billion project'. The record shows: that is the total for Qatari Diar's Simaisma masterplan. The Trump Organization's role is brand licensing via Dar Global.
Claimed: '$5 billion' for the 2026 sales. The record shows: they are $4.01B (Patriot) plus $992.4M (APKWS), approved under an emergency waiver tied to the Iran war.
The 'favorable terms' claim could not be corroborated.
denials_and_context: The White House and Trump say the jet went to the US Air Force, not to Trump personally. Leavitt said it complied fully with the law, and a Bondi legal analysis reportedly found no Emoluments Clause problem.
Qatar first called the transfer 'under consideration' between defence ministries and disputed that it was a gift.
Eric Trump said the Trump Organization has 'zero relationship' with Qatari Diar. Mother Jones noted his own press release praised a 'collaboration with Qatari Diar and Dar Global.'
Critics including Sen. Schumer, Sen. Jack Reed and Norman Eisen called the jet an ethics and emoluments problem.

The 2026 sales followed Iranian strikes on Gulf states. No source links them to Trump business interests, and Isaac Saul of Tangle News, the journalist who drew the connection, himself says 'maybe it's all coincidence.'

changes: No factual changes. The DSCA notice and the Federal Register confirm 26 Mar 2025 and $1.96B ($0.34B MDE plus $1.62B other). The Federal Register (2026-10937) confirms the $992.4M APKWS-II notice for Qatar, delivered to Congress on 1 May 2026, alongside the $4.01B Patriot sale. Israel received an identical $992.4M APKWS package in the same tranche, and some outlets mixed the two up. Trump's first flight on the retrofitted jet was on 1 Jul 2026. These are DSCA notifications, not final contracts.
